title: White Garlic Chicken Pizza
seoTitle: White Garlic Chicken Pizza | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Creamy white pie, roasted garlic
description: Creamy white pie, roasted garlic. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for White Garlic Chicken Pizza in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Roast garlic and wilt spinach
steps.instruction: Toss spinach with a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt; wilt in a hot skillet 2 minutes until collapsed. Squeeze out excess water — wet spinach steams the crust. Set aside.

steps.title: Make garlic béchamel
steps.instruction: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook minced garlic 1 minute until fragrant but not brown. Whisk in flour 1 minute, then milk in steady streams until smooth. Simmer until thick enough to coat a spoon. Off heat, stir in half the parmesan, salt, pepper, and Italian seasoning. Cool 5 minutes — hot white sauce melts raw dough.

steps.title: Preheat stone to 500°F
steps.instruction: Heat pizza stone or steel at 500°F at least 40 minutes. Tear mozzarella and measure ricotta while the oven saturates. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Stretch and white-sauce the pies
steps.instruction: Stretch dough to 12–14 inch rounds with a ½ inch rim. Spread a thin layer of garlic white sauce — you should still see dough in spots. Top with mozzarella, sliced chicken, wilted spinach, ricotta dollops, and remaining parmesan.

steps.title: Bake until golden and set
steps.instruction: Bake 11–14 minutes until cheese browns in spots and the underside is crisp. White pies need color on top and bottom — pale centers mean underbaked dough. Rotate once if the back of the oven runs hot.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion White Garlic Chicken Pizza onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Rest and serve white garlic chicken
steps.instruction: Rest 2 minutes, then cut into 8 slices per pie. White Garlic Chicken Pizza — creamy sauce, roasted garlic flavor, chicken and spinach. Not red-sauce night; keep backup pies on racks at 200°F.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up White Garlic Chicken Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Creamy white pie, roasted garlic. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — White Garlic Chicken Pizza runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
